title: Understanding the error
text: You cannot cancel exponents! $$\frac{a**c}{b**c}\neq$$ $$\frac{a}{b}$$. For example, $$\frac{1^2}{2^2}=\frac{1}{4}$$ is not equal to $$\frac{1}{2}$$.

title: Understanding the error
text: Numbers in bases cannot move into exponents. $$\frac{a**c}{b**c}\neq a**{c-b},$$ For example, $$\frac14=\frac{1**2}{2**2}\neq 1**{2-2}=1**0=1.$$

title: Understanding the error
text: $$\frac{\sqrt[n]{a}}{\sqrt[n]{b}}=\sqrt[n]{a}-\sqrt[n]{b}$$ is mixing up laws of exponents and laws of logarithms. For example, consider $$\frac{\sqrt{1}}{\sqrt{4}}=\frac{1}{2},$$ but $$\sqrt{1}-\sqrt{4}=-1.$$

title: Understanding the correct choice
text: $$\frac{a**c}{b**c}=\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)**c$$ is the law of exponents for quotients with the same exponent and different bases.
